A brilliant rearguard effort from Afghanistan to salvage a draw. Bangladesh were the favourites but their catching and fielding let them down in key moments

17:13 Local Time, 13:13 GMT, 18:43 IST: What a game we have witnessed! Jubilant faces in the Afghan camp while there are dejected ones in the Bangladesh one. Bangladesh have themselves to blame. They dropped a few catches and missed a couple of run-outs in the last session to let the game drift away. The rub of the green also didn't go their way. They couldn't hold onto their nerves when it mattered the most. Kudos to the Afghanistan team. They are known for being warriors and their resilience shone through under testing circumstances. The visitors had nearly five sessions to bowl the hosts out but couldn't breach them. Agreed that the surface was nowhere near a real turner which we usually get to see in UAE but credit needs to be given where it's due. Earlier in the game, fifties upfront from Tanzid and Shadman set things up for the visitors while a fifty down the order from Litton helped them to reach a decent total.

In response, the Afghan batters were insipid apart from Abdul Malik and Rahmat Shah. The Afghan skipper in particular batted beautifully to raise a century. Hasan Mahmud's 5-fer which included a hat-trick enabled the visitors to take a sizeable 106-run lead. Bangladesh were in some trouble in their second essay but fifties from Shanto and Mushfiqur and a century from Litton helped them regain their foothold on the game. They declared and set a mammoth 479 target in front of the hosts. Atal was the star of the show as he batted for more than four sessions. He showed great temperament to raise his maiden Test century and was the key that led the hosts to draw this game. Alikhil's gutsy knock, Ahmadzai's resilience and Qais Ahmad's unconventional batting saved the day for Afghanistan. If the visitors had taken their chances especially in the last hour, it would have been a different story. Stick around for the presentations...

Litton Das | Player of the Match (1/2): (On how difficult it is to keep wickets in the Abu Dhabi heat?) It's really tough because of the heat. Playing in a five-day Test like this, it's really tough as a batsman and wicketkeeper. But I thought that I just need my energy to keep wickets in this heat. If I focus, then it will happen, something good. Yeah, obviously we wanted to win the match, but that's how cricket goes on. Afghanistan played really well. Although the wicket was a little bit flat, the way they batted, on day 4 and day 5, it looked good.

Litton Das (2/2): (On the highlight of his batting?) To be honest, when I got my first run, I was relieved, and I felt that. The thing is, I practised one net session, and I felt that I had some confidence coming back. When I got one run, after that I felt that this gave me a little bit of confidence. The wicket was a little bit flat. I missed out in the first innings. It will be hard for me because every day doesn't give you that much opportunity to score big. But when I went to the second innings, I took that chance. (On his most pleasing catch?) I think Hasan's second wicket in the hat-trick one, because when someone is bowling a short ball, you have time to react. And when someone is bowling outside off, I know it is coming to the right-hand side. That one was tough.

Najmul Hossain Shanto (2/2): (On Litton Das' impressive performance) It’s truly outstanding what Litton achieved in this match. But honestly, it’s not just this game, over the last few years, he’s been exceptional both behind the stumps and with his DRS calls. Showing that kind of character to score a century in these conditions and then keep wickets for 140 overs is incredible. It shows immense strength of character, and I hope he continues this fine form with both bat and gloves. (On Hasan Mahmud and Bangladesh's pace battery) Whenever I throw him (Hasan) the ball, he delivers for the team, regardless of the conditions, whether in Australia or here in the sub-continent. He’s been outstanding, and alongside Ebadot, Taskin, Nahid Rana, and Shoriful, our entire pace unit is doing a tremendous job. They work incredibly hard, and I hope they keep building on this momentum in the years to come.

Rahmat Shah (Afghanistan captain) (1/2): (Is this draw as good as a win for them?) Absolutely. For me, this is a winning moment. The way we put in the effort over five days, whether in bowling or batting, makes it special. (On the resilience from their batters) Absolutely. If you look at it, we had a plan for the game, both in bowling and batting, and we stuck to that plan. If we needed runs, we scored runs. If we needed to spend time at the crease, we spent time at the crease. Because of that, the result moved towards a draw.

Rahmat Shah (2/2): (On Sediqullah’s century and the maturity that he displayed) Sediq has only recently come into the T20 setup, and he showed tremendous temperament. He followed the team's requirements and carried out what was asked of him, and that helped us achieve this result. (On scoring a hundred on debut as an Afghanistan Test captain) As a captain, leading from the front, you have to assess the conditions, the opposition and the bowlers, and use your footwork accordingly. In my opinion, you have to read the opposition fielders and the captain's changes, adjust your batting, and find the gaps to score runs. I worked on my footwork, and that helped me keep adding runs to the board and make the most of the opportunities.
